{"@type": "WebPage", "author": {"name": "Siddharth Shekhar Yadav", "url": "https://uk.linkedin.com/in/sidocean", "@type": "Person", "interactionStatistic": {"@type": "InteractionCounter", "interactionType": "http://schema.org/FollowAction", "userInteractionCount": 12753}}, "headline": "Next week, the United Nations will host the resumed 5th Session on the High Seas Treaty 🌊 - the new UN Treaty on the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction (#BBNJ Treaty).

Check out these 2 papers on BBNJ and resilience by Kristina Gjerde and myself:  

1. ‘The Ocean, Climate Change and Resilience: Making ocean areas beyond national jurisdiction more resilient to climate change and other anthropogenic activities’. This article aims to provide ways of enhancing resilience of marine ecosystems as well as their governance systems, by applying the principles for building socio-ecological resilience (developed by the Stockholm Resilience Centre) to high seas governance and management. 
Link:  https://lnkd.in/efav7ew

  2. ‘Polycentricity and Regional Ocean Governance: Implications for the Emerging UN Agreement on Marine Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction’. Based on a study of polycentric governance theory and regional ocean governance mechanisms, combined with the prior analysis applying resilience principles for socio-ecological systems to ocean ABNJ in Yadav and Gjerde (2020), this new article - Gjerde and Yadav (2021) - highlights ways in which the emerging BBNJ Agreement could stimulate coordinated and integrated action at both global and regional levels.  
Link:  https://lnkd.in/e43fwj8p
 
A BBNJ treaty based on principles and approaches to safeguard resilience could help marine ecosystems and biodiversity cope with #climatechange, other pressures, uncertainty and rapid change in ABNJ, as well as improve the effectiveness of management activities.  

See you at the UN next week.

Exploring the Technology’s Potential for Sustainable Development.

Agri-food supply chains are complex and involve a large number of actors — from small-scale farmers, primary processors, and traders to product manufacturers, distributors, retailers, and consumers. This complexity limits farm-to-table traceability, which is key to identify sustainability-related issues in agri-food systems including extreme inequality and poverty, human rights violations, and environmental degradation.

Blockchain for Agri-Food Traceability explores the technology’s potential in advancing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) related to the agri-food sector, leveraging its unique features like its decentralised nature, immutability of data, and smart contracts. The report also highlights key considerations for implementing an end-to-end traceability system that is scalable, sustainable, and inclusive, ensuring that the most disadvantaged stakeholders, the small-scale producers are not left behind.

Riad Meddeb

caption:
Youth are the future of innovation for our climate and oceans. By supporting our youth as leaders of digital transformation and climate action, we can strengthen our communities at their foundations and build the next generation of leaders and innovators.
 
The global Youth4Climate Initiative has released a call for innovative ideas for young people and youth organizations to take climate action, with grants up to 20,000 USD alongside mentorship and capacity-building. There are four thematic areas: food and agriculture ,energy, education and urban sustainability. Apply here by March 31st, and please share with your communities 👉https://lnkd.in/dgC6nHia
 
Youth4Climate brings together existing and new online and offline resources, tools, capacities, partnerships, networks, and movements by and for youth, with a strong focus on implementation, for more sustained impact on climate on the ground. You can also register to the Youth4Climate Platform here 👉https://lnkd.in/dYfG24Dk

Agostino Inguscio Adam Rogers James Ellsmoor 🏝️ James Alix Michel  Connect4Climate Rome Centre UNDP Enrico Gaveglia Snehal V Soneji Amanda K. S. Ulrika Modeer UNDP Marina Orruela Monteoliva

{"@type": "WebPage", "author": {"name": "Calum Handforth", "image": {"url": "https://media.licdn.com/dms/image/v2/D4E03AQHvu63Snsy6Aw/profile-displayphoto-scale_400_400/B4EaA_o2gdKoBY-/0/1787774070934?e=2147483647&v=beta&t=N69sTiFuQE2oAeF8_sOMmob0LZNAWjyb3jYynk_RNT8", "@type": "ImageObject"}, "url": "https://uk.linkedin.com/in/calumhandforth", "@type": "Person", "interactionStatistic": {"@type": "InteractionCounter", "interactionType": "http://schema.org/FollowAction", "userInteractionCount": 7616}}, "headline": "Excited to share my MIT Technology Review piece, co-authored with Riad Meddeb, advocating for the importance of redefining #SmartCities.

Do an online image search for 'smart cities' - and you'll see the same pictures. Page after page of high-tech, sensor-driven cities - with light trails, laser beams, and technology symbols floating in the ether. The 'components' of a smart city. What is missing, though, are the components of an actual city: people, communities, and nature - lives and livelihoods.

Cities are more than 5G, Big Data, driverless vehicles, and AI. But this tech-centricity unfairly focuses attention on one type of urban development, and distracts from the importance of inclusive and sustainable urbanisation. This is a particular risk in places where high-tech 'smart' cities are financially, logistically, and otherwise irrelevant.

We need to make cities work for people. Particularly when 68% of the global population will be living in urban areas by 2050. These are the drivers for the Smart Cities work at UNDP and UNDP Global Centre, Singapore - including highlighting that a 'smart' city is about much more than the latest technology. 

We need smarter cities, and fewer 'smart cities'. Read our article here ➡️ https://lnkd.in/du4n4kE7

What makes your city #smart?

(We also explore more about smartness in the Smart Urban Innovations Handbook - including the role of high-tech, low-tech, and no-tech in cities. Available on the UNDP site!)."}

{"@type": "WebPage", "author": {"name": "Barbados Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade", "image": {"url": "https://media.licdn.com/dms/image/v2/C4D0BAQFvj16NyqgA9w/company-logo_100_100/company-logo_100_100/0/1630560793596?e=2147483647&v=beta&t=u5tyN9Tx4sCG9knK_l-asa2-swYeF3EdscJX0GrWJrA", "@type": "ImageObject"}, "url": "https://bb.linkedin.com/company/barbados-ministry-of-foreign-affairs-and-foreign-trade", "@type": "Organization", "interactionStatistic": {"@type": "InteractionCounter", "interactionType": "http://schema.org/FollowAction", "userInteractionCount": 22767}}, "headline": "Bridgetown Initiative 2.0 Highlights Six Key Action Areas

The United Nations Secretary-General and the Prime Minister of Barbados joined forces under the Bridgetown Initiative to address the immediate needs of countries facing debt distress and liquidity challenges, proposing a large-scale SDG Stimulus package to invest in the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), while stressing the need for reform of the international financial architecture.

According to the 2023 Financing for Sustainable Development Report, 52 low- and middle-income developing economies are either in debt distress or at high risk of debt distress, accounting for more than 40% of the world’s poorest people.

“The international financial architecture is short-sighted, crisis-prone, and bears no relation to the economic reality of today,” said UN Secretary-General António Guterres.

Convened at the UN Headquarters in New York by Secretary-General António Guterres and Prime Minister Mia Amor Mottley, participants included experts from academia, civil society and national governments. They considered concrete actions to advance immediate game-changing steps and longer-term reform.

“The world is running out of time to fix its international financial system that is broken, outdated, infested with short-termism and downright unfair. Too many countries are being prevented from fighting the climate crisis and from creating decent opportunities for billions of people – their citizens. If countries cannot access the finance they need at rates they can afford, the world will lose the battle, not simply the countries. What is good for the North is good for the South, East and West! This is the best development strategy for the people of the developing world. This is the best development strategy for the planet,” said Prime Minister Mia Amor Mottley of Barbados.

Deliberations highlighted an international financial system that is not fit for purpose, with developing countries facing debt overhangs, higher borrowing costs and limited access to liquidity in times of crisis. In turn, developing economies cannot fund progress on the SDGs, including climate adaptation, if they are borrowing at up to 14 percent while also paying more than 20 percent of revenue for debt servicing.

A short intro piece from Benjamin Bertelsen and me, on why DPI is important - and key considerations for governments. A few takeaways:

💡 DPI is an approach to digital transformation that emphasises open solutions, open standards and open protocols.
💡 Countries with DPI components may be more able to support their populations than countries without these digital foundations.
💡 Beyond foundational digital public infrastructure, DPI tackling key themes or sectors could also have impact - including in areas like health, climate, or finance. For example, implementing DPI in the #justice system could expand access to justice for more than 50 million additional people by 2030. Whilst DPI for tackling #carbon emissions could speed up the rate of reducing emissions by more than five years in some countries.

Dans le document que je remets en lien ci-dessous, j'explique pourquoi il est urgent que la collectivité reprenne le contrôle de l'innovation, pour que son sens ne soit pas plus exclusivement détermé par ceux qui détiennent le pouvoir (économique et politique). Je suis d'autant plus convaincu par cela que j ai découvert le tout récent livre de Acemoglu et Simon Johnson "Power and Progress" qui vont en profondeur dans ce sujet (j'en suis au début).

	Proposition 17 « Principes directeurs pour un nouveau système d’innovation »
Un préalable est de tracer les contours d’un nouveau modèle de bien-être. Ceci est fondamental, car c’est cela qui donnera une orientation à l’innovation. Par exemple, opter pour un modèle encore basé sur la croissance, mais « verte », est assez différent d’un modèle qui repose sur un bien être moins dépendant du matériel et l’accumulation.  
A.     Economie de ressources et d’énergie : les innovations qui nous poussent à accroître notre pression extractive sur la nature ne peuvent pas être encouragées si nous voulons réduire notre pression extractive.
B.     Préservation de la biosphère : compte tenu de son importance pour l’humanité, il parait critique de passer au filtre « biosphère » les innovations.
C.     Travail et dignité humaine : les innovations qui dépossèdent, à grande échelle, l’être humain de la valeur travail ne sont pas compatibles avec un monde post-croissance[1].
D.    Démocratie : les innovations majeures, c’est-à-dire qui sont susceptibles d’avoir un impact systémique, doivent être discutées dans un cadre démocratique. Il faut aussi un encadrement démocratique des nouvelles technologies, notamment les technologies numériques. 
o  Par exemple, l’AI est d’une grande utilité dans certains domaines, mais en complément du travail humain pas en parfait substitut. Par ailleurs, l’application de l’AI sans limites est incompatible avec la préservation de nombreux « facteurs » essentiels comme la démocratie elle-même.

Sur cette base, il est possible de définir un cahier des charges plus précis avec un système de « scoring » qui nous permettrait par exemple "d’interdire" le soutien public à certaines innovations, et plus généralement de définir des politiques publiques qui permettent de mieux l’orienter.

  [1] Le monde post-croissance sera un monde dans lequel le travail « humain » sera plus important. #innovation #travail #power #changementclimatique"}

caption:
🌍 Inspired by the Youth4Climate: #SparkingSolutions Event
 
Last week, I had the privilege of being part of the selection panel for the Energy thematic at the Youth4Climate: Sparking Solutions event in Rome. Witnessing the passion, dedication, and innovative spirit of the youth presenting their energy projects was truly remarkable.
 
Gathering from 63 countries, these young minds came together with a 100 youth-driven solutions, all with a shared goal of creating a meaningful impact on our planet. The level of creativity and thoughtfulness in their projects was truly impressive.
 
At the event, I had the honor of witnessing some incredible project pitches from the youth. These innovative solutions included ideas such as harnessing affordable and renewable heating sources like Biomass, a high-performing stove that can save up to 5 tons of CO2 emissions, and initiatives to promote the use of solar power in off-grid schools and community centres. These ideas are not only impressive but also represent tangible steps towards reducing our carbon footprint and promoting #cleanenergy solutions. It's a testament to their dedication and ingenuity.
 
Taking part in the #Youth4Climate event reaffirmed my conviction: the future of our planet is in the hands of the next generation, and they are ready to take on the challenge. But we need to empower them, provide the support they need, and enable them to implement  their ideas so that #sustainableenergy use becomes the norm, not the exception.
 
The #Youth4Climate initiative, co-led by the UNDP Rome Centre  and Ministero dell'Ambiente e della Sicurezza Energetica  funding, mentorship programs, and capacity-building opportunities, these young climate leaders will have the tools to turn their innovative ideas into reality.

#EnergyForDevelopment 
 
UNDP Agostino Inguscio Ulrika Modeer Haoliang Xu Cassie Flynn Simone Marino Calum Handforth Piyush Verma Francesco Corvaro

In just 10 days, we're unveiling the @UNDP Energy Governance Framework! 🌐
 
🗓️ Save the Date: November 15th, 10:30 am ET ⏰
 
Join us as we gather an impressive lineup of speakers to explore the future of energy governance for a just energy transition. Don't miss this opportunity to be part of this very important conversation! 🌍🔌
Mark your calendars, set your alarms, and get ready to be inspired. Together, we'll shape a greener, more sustainable world for all. 🌿💡
 
Note the speakers:
 
1. Ms. Vandana Gombar, Senior Editor – BloombergNEF (Moderator)
2. Mr. Marcos Neto, ASG, Assistant Administrator and Director, BPPS-UNDP (Introductory Remarks)
3. H.E. Victor Parlicov, Minister of Energy, Republic of Moldova
4. H.E. Edgar Moyo, Minister of Energy and Power Development, Zimbabwe
5. H.E. Ambassador Ruchira Kamboj, India’s Permanent Representative. to the United Nations
6. Ms. Rosilena Lindo, Deputy Energy Secretary, Panama
7. Mr. Roger Martella, Group VP, General Electric, and Chief Sustainability Officer, GE Vernova
8. Ms. Teresa Kramarz, Co-Director of Environmental Governance, University of Toronto, Canada
 
Register for the event at: https://lnkd.in/epbA-uJN
 
#UNDP #EnergyGovernance #justenergytransition #enegyfordevelopment

caption:
Delighted to have delivered a keynote at the Round Table Discussion, organized by ISA with the EU and SolarPower Europe, on transforming Africa through sustainable energy & partnerships, where I emphasized the urgent need to evolve our financing approach to address disparities in clean energy finance in Africa.

Currently, investments are unevenly distributed, with ten nations accounting for 90% of private energy infrastructure investment. This leaves annual financing needs for energy access initiatives far short of the required $25B USD to achieve the 2030 objectives. In 2024, an estimated $110B USD will be invested in energy across Africa, with $70B allocated to fossil fuels and only 35% to clean energy technologies.

In my address, I highlighted the three key levers for systemic transformation:

1. To shift the focus of finance at the national level, which still prioritizes risks to lenders over the greater risk that climate change poses to people & the planet.
2. Changing the macro-level financial system to facilitate access to capital in critical geographies and sectors.
3. Optimizing energy systems with AI-driven solutions to boost renewable energy investment where its needed most.

Around 60 million people in Africa 🌍access electricity via off-grid solutions, with 15 countries using distributed renewables in their electrification plans. Scaling renewable, decentralized, and affordable energy systems can drive inclusive development.

Establishing robust financial models and fostering public-private partnerships are key to unlocking the $200 billion annual investment needed by 2030 for Africa's energy, climate, and development goals.

#EnergyForDevelopment ⚡️

Excellent meeting with H.E. Honourable Hamada Moussa, Comoros' Minister of Energy, at the Africa Energy Forum to discuss how Comoros is diversifying its economy and strengthening its productive capacity through renewable energy.

Energy plays a crucial role in catalyzing the Antigua and Barbuda Agenda for SIDS (ABAS) - a renewed declaration to deliver meaningful change and resilience in Small Island Developing States.

UNDP is supporting Comoros' transition by developing policies and frameworks to tap into geothermal and other natural resources for sustainable energy.

Delighted to have participated in the ‘Let’s Talk Data’ event with experts from @worldbank, @universityofmichigan, and @UNDP. 

I emphasized on the human angle of sustainable energy for development, and the need to go beyond collecting data, making these findings actionable for amplifying our impact on the ground:

* Energy poverty affects health, social inclusion, and economic opportunities. We must prioritize data and indicators that include social, environmental and development dimensions
* Open energy modeling tools need to better incorporate social and development factors beyond market dynamics. We must invest in data infrastructure to address urban-rural disparities, informal energy markets, economic transitions, and disaggregated demographic data.
* Effective energy policies and interventions require precise, actionable insights derived from high-resolution geospatial data and advanced analytics, enabling equitable interventions to ensure renewable energy benefits reach all communities, especially underserved areas

At @UNDP, our focus remains on leveraging technology and data combined with an integrated development approach to achieve #SDG7 🌍 

Learn more 👉🏼 hrea.isr.umich.edu/ 💡
Damilola Ogunbiyi Marco Gervasi Marcos Neto International Energy Agency (IEA) Agostino Inguscio

caption:
The severe floods in Pakistan in 2022 damaged 22 power plants and caused outages and load shedding of up to 16 hours. 

In the face of severe climate change, we must leverage the power of digital technologies and innovation to ensure energy resilience and security. Here is how:

* Smart grids and AI-driven storage enhance grid stability, reliability, and efficiency
* Advanced analytics and smart meters optimize energy use, empowering consumers with real-time data for more efficient consumption and cost savings
* IoT and Digital Twins (DT) provide real-time monitoring and proactive maintenance, ensuring infrastructure resilience and rapid response to extreme weather events

We discuss these strategies focusing on energy security in the latest issue of Development Advocate Pakistan — read the publication for an excellent collection of articles and thought leadership 👉🏼 
https://lnkd.in/eTMXz5Jv 💡
Mahenau Agha Marcos Neto Damilola Ogunbiyi Kanni Wignaraja

1.⁠ Develop regulatory frameworks, enhance skills training for workers, and create targeted support systems to ensure a just transition
2.⁠ ⁠Scale sustainable finance through supportive policies that unlock investment in renewables and enhance energy efficiency
3.⁠ ⁠Leverage digital innovation and AI to optimize systems and enable data-driven policymaking within broader socio-economic contexts

This journey will be driven by the convergence of digitalization, market development, policy, and governance. 💡

#EnergyForDevelopment ⚡️

caption:
Delighted to have contributed to an inspiring session on The Road to COP29: Island Priorities for Baku hosted by @Island Innovation. It was an excellent opportunity to emphasize how the energy transition in #SIDS can build resilience and unlock economic opportunities while discussing the key role of youth, and actionable steps to drive this shift: 

1.⁠ ⁠Establish a finance framework that provides debt relief & removes financial barriers, utilizing innovative tools like debt-for-energy swaps
2.⁠ ⁠Harness digital transformation to improve data availability, enabling infrastructure deployment and management tailored to each island community 
3.⁠ ⁠Implement a whole-island approach that integrates renewables with the blue economy to support economic diversification

Nearly 60% of SIDS’ population is under 30, making #youth the driving force of sustainable energy innovation in #SIDS. On the road to #COP29, we must work with them to create environments that empower their leadership, ensuring the convergence of all efforts toward enabling SIDS to proactively define their energy-for-development pathways. ☀️🌊🏝️

#EnergyForDevelopment ⚡️#RisingUpForSIDS

caption:
The #PactForTheFuture has been adopted, positioning energy access and security as essential for economic development, social stability, and achieving our Development Goals. It calls for urgent action to mobilize finance at scale to ensure affordable, reliable, and sustainable energy for all, alongside investments in resilient cross-border energy infrastructure.

Unlocking the scale of private investment in clean energy will require policy de-risking mechanisms to enhance the financial viability of renewable projects, incentivizing private capital, affordable tariffs, and expanded energy services. Given that 40% of low- and middle-income countries are facing severe debt issues, targeted financial flows and equitable redistribution are essential for accelerating renewable energy deployment in the Global South.

#Digital, AI, and data hold immense potential to meet these goals by guiding financing towards impactful solutions through data-driven insights.

Learn about the actionable steps to ensure that #OurCommonFuture leverages #digital to accelerate the finance needed to drive progress for our energy, climate, and development goals. 🌱💡 👉 bit.ly/SEH-Energy-Digital

India’s unique energy transition highlights how a nation can balance growing energy demand with the need for reliable access and sustainability. Since 2000, half a billion people have gained access to electricity, and India has become the 4th largest renewable energy producer globally.

I am pleased to have joined a great session during the #SDG7 Action Forum, with Jessica Seddon, Soumya Swaminathan  Rishika Das Roy  William Brent  Abhishek Jain, and Arunabha Ghosh  highlighting India’s energy transition and the important lessons that can guide other nations in their own energy journeys. 💡

Disruptive approaches are needed to accelerate a just energy transition:

1. Leverage an integrated approach of policy, market development and digital innovation 
2. Integrated energy governance - engaging communities in decision making processes and support gender responsive policies
3. Develop strong policy reforms for transformative changes such as fossil fuel subsidies reforms to renewables and e-mobility

How can we learn from other countries' transition pathways and tailor these approaches to our interventions? 💡

At UNDP, we draw on India’s experience to support nations globally, particularly in Africa, helping advance decentralized energy solutions and enable a just transition for coal-dependent regions.

During the #SDG7 Action Forum, I had the honor of opening a session on clean cooking alongside partners from the The World Bank  World Health Organization, Sustainable Energy for All (SEforALL)   and @UNDESA.

I emphasized four critical actions we must take to ensure we don't lose momentum on clean cooking.

•⁠  ⁠First, integrate clean cooking into energy transition, climate, and development policies, ensuring alignment with electrification and national goals.
•⁠  ⁠Second, strengthen finance access through capacity building, innovation, and private sector collaboration.
•⁠  ⁠⁠Third, tailor solutions to local needs and promote job creation by understanding consumer behaviors
•⁠  ⁠⁠Fourth, leverage data insights and blended finance models to de-risk investments, making clean cooking more attractive to investors.

By focusing on these actions, we can achieve tangible progress on clean cooking & drive the global shift towards a just and inclusive energy transition.

#EnergyForDevelopment #UNGA

Honored to participate at the 3rd Iran Energy Efficiency Conference and Exhibition on enhancing #energyefficiency and optimizing consumption to drive sustainable development.

Three key priorities emerged:

1.⁠ ⁠Mobilize investment in energy efficiency across buildings, industry, and transport, including achieving 10,000 MW of energy savings by 2030 through energy efficiency measures
2.⁠ ⁠Advance renewable energy initiatives in line with Iran’s target of 30,000 MW by 2030, with a focus on electrification in big cities like Tehran through electric vehicles (EVs)
3.⁠ ⁠Empower Iran’s workforce by integrating energy efficiency and renewables, creating green jobs and unlocking opportunities for over 230,000 engineers entering the workforce each year

With the right policies and a prepared workforce, #Iran could unlock up to $2 trillion in annual savings by 2030, reduce energy intensity by 31%, and transform its economy. This transformative shift will support Iran's 2025 Vision for a sustainable and secure energy future.

#EnergyForDevelopment ⚡️

caption:
At the 2024 Seoul Debates on "Leveraging Innovation for Sustainable and Low-Carbon Energy," I had the opportunity to moderate a disruptive conversation. The event featured welcoming words from Dr. Anne Juepner  Director of UNDP Seoul Policy Centre  H.E. Insun Kang, 2nd Vice Minister of Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Republic of Korea  and Mr. Achim Steiner  UNDP  Administrator—all highlighting the crucial need for collective and truly innovative solutions to our world’s climate challenges.

Sharing the stage with esteemed panelists—Mr. Seunghyo Choi from Korea's Ministry of Trade, Industry, and Energy; Ms. Gothami Gannoruwa  from Sri Lanka's Ministry of Power and Energy; Ms. Kim Hee of POSCO  Holdings; and Dr. Semee Yoon  from @‌Seoul National University—we delved into how digitalization and innovation can transform the sustainable energy landscape. The discussions covered policy incentives, impacts on rural energy access, private sector innovations in energy efficiency, and academia's role in bridging technology and policy.

In my opening remarks, I emphasized three key points: the transformative convergence of the data revolution with renewable energy, the imperative of embedding innovation into the very fabric of our sustainable energy systems, and the advancement of inclusive technologies to bridge innovation gaps. ⚡️

Watch the full recording 👉 https://lnkd.in/eH_a5rKT

As the next generation of leaders, youth have a key role in this transformation—their creativity and forward-thinking approaches will be key in shaping just energy solutions that reach everyone, everywhere. 🌏

caption:
As COP16 Colombia  on biodiversity begins, we have an opportunity to show how renewable energy can support both climate action and biodiversity conservation.

Scaling up renewable energy is imperative for mitigating climate change, and with careful planning, it can enhance biodiversity protection. By deploying renewable solutions like wind, solar, and photovoltaics that incorporate biomimicry—mimicking natural processes such as the efficiency of photosynthesis—we can create energy nature-based solutions that harmonize with local habitats, solving electricity access challenges while safeguarding ecosystems. 🌱

Through strategic environmental assessments, renewable energy projects can do more than just power communities—they can reduce carbon emissions, protect habitats, and minimize disruption to fragile ecosystems. This dual approach enables us to tackle the climate and biodiversity crises together, aligning with our Kunming-Montreal Framework commitments. 🌳

Read here about 4 ways to mainstream biodiversity into renewable #energy ⚡️planning 👇

#COP16 #PazConLaNaturaleza #PeaceWithNature #ForPeopleForPlanet #EnergyForDevelopment

As COP16 Colombia  on biodiversity begins, we have an opportunity to show how renewable energy can support both climate action and biodiversity conservation.

Scaling up renewable energy is imperative for mitigating climate change, and with careful planning, it can enhance biodiversity protection. By deploying renewable solutions like wind, solar, and photovoltaics that incorporate biomimicry—mimicking natural processes such as the efficiency of photosynthesis—we can create energy nature-based solutions that harmonize with local habitats, solving electricity access challenges while safeguarding ecosystems. 🌱

Through strategic environmental assessments, renewable energy projects can do more than just power communities—they can reduce carbon emissions, protect habitats, and minimize disruption to fragile ecosystems. This dual approach enables us to tackle the climate and biodiversity crises together, aligning with our Kunming-Montreal Framework commitments. 🌳

Read here about 4 ways to mainstream biodiversity into renewable #energy ⚡️planning 👇

#COP16 #PazConLaNaturaleza #PeaceWithNature #ForPeopleForPlanet #EnergyForDevelopment

As we approach #COP29, it’s imperative that initiatives like this are highlighted and used as blueprints for action—contributing toward both climate change mitigation and sustainable development. 🌍

In a major step toward healthcare resilience, UNDP  Zimbabwe and the The Global Fund  have equipped 1,044 health facilities across Zimbabwe with solar systems, with a combined generation capacity exceeding 11 MW. 🏥

This renewable energy solution ensures consistent power for rural clinics, enabling them to refrigerate vaccines, run essential medical equipment, and deliver uninterrupted patient care—even during power outages. By reducing grid dependency, this project addresses energy poverty and enhances healthcare access for underserved communities across Zimbabwe. 💡

Other key benefits of the solar project include:

1. Energy Efficiency: Solar systems provide up to 70% of electricity needs, reducing reliance on the grid.
2. Environmental Impact: Over 11,447 tons of CO2 emissions will be avoided annually.
3. Cost Savings: Cuts electricity and diesel costs, allowing more resources for healthcare services.

caption:
60% of electricity in Latin America and the Caribbean is already generated from #renewables, double the global average. With abundant hydropower, solar PV, and wind potential, along with 60% of the world’s lithium reserves essential for battery technology, the region has the capacity to leverage this transition to redefine sustainable development while securing local benefits for its communities. 

Moreover, this shift also promises employment opportunities, with #energy sector jobs projected to increase by over 15% by 2030, particularly in clean energy technologies and in the critical mineral sector. This momentum positions LAC to aim even higher by 2030, and even more ambitious goals than currently set in national targets can be made possible through strengthened cooperation, financial mobilization, innovative policy, and digital advancements, which will be essential building blocks for what could be a “second generation of the energy transition.” 

This approach can extend beyond energy production to include key areas like transport electrification and sustainable mining, positioning LAC as a global blueprint for just energy transitions at scale. With COP16 and the Latin American Energy Organization (OLADE) Energy Week now underway, LAC can maintain and accelerate their momentum toward a sustainable, resilient future powered by clean energy.

Explore further in our newest Sustainable Energy Bulletin on Latin America and the Caribbean  👉https://lnkd.in/ehKr25hQ

caption:
One year ago, at COP28 UAE  we set the ambitious target of tripling renewable energy capacity and doubling energy efficiency by 2030. Today, at COP29 Azerbaijan  the urgency to shift from ambition to action is evident.
On the sidelines of #COP29, I joined a key discussion on how to unlock Africa’s energy potential to drive sustainable development, a session co-organized by UNDP  and the Italian Presidency of the #G7. 🫱🏽‍🫲🏼

Three key catalysts emerged:
1.	Streamline policy regulations and provide technical assistance to advance more projects to financial closure, building a pipeline of scalable, bankable projects.
2.	Innovative guarantee schemes to address financial barriers by providing a safety net to investors and lenders, encouraging investment by reducing perceived risks.
3.	 Leverage #digital to optimize energy systems, reduce costs, and attract private investment by increasing data availability, and the scalability and resilience of renewables infrastructure.

We spotlighted the” Energy for Growth in Africa” initiative—a strategic partnership between UNDP, the Italian Government, and the #G7—aimed at catalyzing Africa’s clean energy transformation through strategic investment, policy support, and multi-stakeholder collaboration. In synergy with initiatives like Mission 300, together, we can mobilize public, private, and development finance to unlock the full potential of Africa’s clean energy revolution. 

@UNDP stands ready to continue supporting Africa’s #SustainableEnergyRevolution⚡️ by de-risking investments, offering policy support, and fostering partnerships to create scalable, bankable energy projects across the continent. 💡
Ministero degli Affari Esteri e della Cooperazione Internazionale, Ministero dell'Ambiente e della Sicurezza Energetica , IAI - Istituto Affari Internazionali  
#G7 #EnergyTransition #EnegyForDevelopment

caption:
Energizing start to #COP29⚡️
It was a pleasure to moderate an excellent discussion on strategies to catalyze private investment for accelerating a just transition, a session on the sidelines of #COP29 co-organized with @UNDP and @UNCDF. 💡
With only 15% of global energy investments reaching developing countries and just 2% directed to Africa, we are at a critical juncture.
Our great round of panelists provided key insights into the urgent need for policy alignment, innovative financing mechanisms, and strategic partnerships to mobilize energy finance for developing nations. 🔅
Key actionable points included:
1. Creating policy environments that reduce investment risk and attract private capital for clean energy.
2. Implementing innovative finance solutions such as blended finance, guarantee schemes and concessional loans to unlock funding for renewable projects.
3. Strengthening global partnerships to bridge the financial gap and support vulnerable economies in achieving their energy goals.

With only 15% of global energy investments reaching developing countries and just 2% directed to Africa, we are at a critical juncture.

Together with United Nations Capital Development Fund (UNCDF)  UNDP  is committed to advancing de-risking financial instruments suited to the scale and risk profile of these transactions. Through synergies with initiatives like Mission 300, Energy for Growth, and AMP, we have the tools, knowledge, and strategies to drive action.

Let’s build on this momentum to catalyze the financing needed to achieve our global energy, climate, and development goals. 🌎
Thank you Stefano Marguccio , Pradeep Kurukulasuriya. 
#SustainableEnergyRevolution⚡️ #EnergyForDevelopment #EnergyTransition

caption:
🌊 SIDS have consistently shown resilience and leadership in protecting their unique cultural and geographic heritage through bold commitments and strong political will, including pledges by many to achieve 100% renewable electricity by 2030.

At @COP29 in Azerbaijan, @UNDP and @AOSIS joined forces to host a session that provided a platform for discussing and positioning actionable opportunities to operationalize the priorities of the ABAS declaration, focusing on how to accelerate a just energy transition to unlock development opportunities in SIDS.

Key action steps to advance the energy-for-development pathway in SIDS: 

1. Advance a just energy transition to unlock transformative development across key sectors such as e-mobility, sustainable tourism, urban agriculture, and fisheries – tailored to the needs of each island community. 🏝️🚌
2. Leverage digital innovation to transition from traditional centralized systems to smart grids and digital platforms that optimize local electricity networks, enhancing resilience and efficiency, particularly in regions prone to natural disasters. 🌱
3. Scale financial mechanisms like debt-for-nature & energy swaps, blended finance funds, and National Laboratories of Financial Innovation to mobilize the capital needed to reach the $5.9 USD billion annually to meet their renewable energy target by 2030.  💡

@UNDP, in partnership with @AOSIS, has introduced a strategic approach addressing the ABAS declaration, detailed in our policy brief, “Advancing a Just Energy Transition in SIDS.” Presented during the event, this paper outlines key sustainable energy opportunities for the next decade of development in SIDS, to drive equitable economic growth and enhance resilience for integrated human development. ⚡️ 

#RisingUpForSIDS🏝️ #SustainableEnergyRevolution⚡️ #EnergyForDevelopment

caption:
In the last year alone, sustainable bonds and funds surpassed $7T, with $205B in green bonds for the energy sector. This is a promising trend, but it is far from enough.

On the sidelines of @COP29 Azerbaijan, I joined an insightful session organized by @‌DAMU Kazakhstan, alongside leading energy and finance experts, where I highlighted three enablers to drive investments for exponential growth:

1. Robust de-risking mechanisms that reduce financial risk and attract private capital to clean energy projects.
2. Innovative finance instruments like blended finance and thematic bonds to mobilize large-scale investments and address market inefficiencies.
3. Strategic use of #digital to enhance investment allocation and ensure data-driven decision-making.

UNDP is a leader on supporting countries to access, channel, and deliver finance towards energy & climate goals. In Kazakhstan, our green finance partnership with DAMU has piloted a suite of green financial tools, including loan interest subsidies and green bonds, which have helped de-risk renewable and low-carbon investments, offering a model that can be scaled.

At #COP29, the conversation needs to include a reformed financial architecture to close the $2.2 trillion annual energy investment gap needed through 2050, ensuring 1.5°C remains achievable and the SDGs are met.

#EnergyForDevelopment #SustainableEnergyRevolution #COP29

caption:
Indonesia, the world's largest archipelagic nation, has made impressive strides in electricity access with a 99.78% rate. Yet, its unique geography of over 17,000 islands presents challenges in reaching remote communities.

It was an insightful discussion at @‌COP29 Azerbaijan in a session with @‌Ministry of Energy and Mineral Resources (ESDM), where I shared strategies for advancing rural electrification in Indonesia and highlighted key steps to ensure energy access leads to improved livelihoods and inclusivity:

💡 Scaling distributed renewable energy and off-grid solutions such as solar micro-grids and stand-alone systems
💡Strengthening policy and regulatory frameworks that guide rural electrification.
💡 Targeted financial support and economic incentives to address access to finance for both end-users and suppliers
💡Ensuring active community participation from project design to maintenance.
💡Promoting women’s leadership in the energy sector, with focused training and capacity-building.

UNDP is committed to advancing these strategies to support Indonesia's energy revolution. By fostering community-driven projects like ACCESS, we aim to turn energy access into a catalyst for sustainable growth and resilience.

Learn how #solar ☀️ is powering economic growth in Indonesia 👉 https://lnkd.in/es6RBvqk

caption:
If scaled effectively, digital technologies could reduce emissions by 20% by 2050 in the energy, materials, and mobility sectors.

How can we leverage #digital to optimize our energy systems and achieve our ambitious climate goals? ⚡️

I joined a panel of experts at KPMG ‘s flagship event at #COP29, to strategize on leveraging the triptych of digital innovation, data, and AI to meet the urgency of the energy transition.

Key takeaways include:

1. Digital, data, and AI hold tremendous potential to increase electricity access, optimize energy systems, improve resilience, and reduce costs and emissions, but only if we ensure that the digital tools we develop are designed to reach the most vulnerable.
2. Transitioning from conventional funding, leveraging blended finance as a catalyst can mobilize significant private capital. This reduces investment risks and unites varied funding sources to drive large-scale renewable projects, particularly in high-risk markets.
3. Developing supportive policies and regulations for advancing digital, digital and data, technologies innovation, and investments will be a key enablers of achieving 2030 goals

This approach, combined with strategic partnerships, people-centered investments and tools, and transparent data practices, will drive a resilient and equitable #SustainableEnergyRevolution. ⚡️

Thank you for a disruptive discussion, Daisy Shen 沈莹  Shen @‌KPMG, Sam Peacock  @‌SSE plc, Liz Henderson  @‌Aon, @dr . Sanjay Kumar Gupta CEO Adani Group  Michael Hayes  KPMG Ireland  Trevor Hutchings  @‌REA, Anish De  @‌KPMG.

caption:
Our collective ambitions to #3xRenewables is critical to keep 1.5°C within reach. However, current NDCs cover only 12% of this target, and with the next round of NDCs due in 2025, this offers an opportunity to place advancing an energy transition as a priority for NDCs. ☀️

On the session “Pathways to Energy Integration in NDCs,” co-hosted by @‌IRENA and @Ocean Conservancy, I highlighted three key opportunities to make NDCs ambitious and actionable, focusing on scaling sustainable renewable energy:

1. Support countries in creating bankable energy projects integrated with their NDCs, ensuring these plans are actionable and backed by comprehensive sectoral investment analyses.
2. ⁠Promote financial innovation & implement tools like credit guarantees and blended finance, facilitating debt-smart energy transition financing in developing countries.
3. ⁠Leverage digital technologies to help identify optimal investment opportunities, ensure optimized off-grid solutions & enable data-driven policymaking.

UNDP  and United Nations Capital Development Fund (UNCDF)  are supporting these efforts by scaling up capital for renewable energy and developing innovative guarantee schemes that provide safety nets for investors and lenders, reducing perceived risks to move renewable energy projects from pipeline to financial closure.

#COP29 COP29 Azerbaijan Noura Hamladji

caption:
With over 600 million people projected to live in vulnerable coastal areas by 2050 and #SIDS 🏝️already facing $153 billion in losses from extreme weather over the last 50 years, the urgency for action is clear. Island nations are not just on the front lines—they are at the forefront of solutions, but supporting their leadership is crucial. 💡🌊

On the sidelines of #COP29, I participated in a seminar focused on building global climate governance through zero-carbon island cooperation. Opened by an insightful keynote speech from Mr. Zheng Deyan, Mayor of Yantai City, the event set the stage for discussing community-led energy models and regional partnerships tailored to island contexts. 

I highlighted the value of scalable, community-centered energy hubs that integrate renewable power with key sectors like sustainable fisheries and tourism. I further emphasized on the critical role of adaptive regulatory frameworks for enabling island states to scale renewable energy projects, align with global climate goals, and enhance economic resilience. ☀️

With the right tools and support, island communities can unlock the power of the energy transition and transform their local leadership into a global model for sustainable progress.

#RisingUpForSIDS🏝️ #SustainableEnergyRevolution⚡️ #EnergyForDevelopment #EnergyTransition

I had the honor of meeting with Cuba’s delegation in #COP29, including key representatives from the Ministry of Energy and Power, to discuss strategic pathways for enhancing Cuba’s energy resilience and accelerating its renewable energy transition. 🇨🇺

Our high-level discussions focused on opportunities to leverage Cuba’s ambitious target of generating 24% of electricity from renewables by 2030. We explored the potential of the Financial Architecture framework, supported by UNDP, as a catalyst for mobilizing both public and private investments. Key components, such as the Financial Innovation Lab (FILAB) and the Investment Accelerator, were emphasized as pivotal in piloting innovative financing mechanisms and fostering bankable, investment-ready projects. 💡

We identified new avenues to enhance access to international climate funds, deepen collaboration with multilateral banks, and utilize concessional and blended finance approaches. Strengthening these strategic partnerships will be essential to navigating Cuba’s energy challenges and seizing opportunities for sustainable energy growth.

caption:
I had the honor of moderating a side event focused on advancing a people-centered energy transition in Eurasia on the sidelines of COP29 Azerbaijan  .Hosted by the UNDP in Europe and Central Asia , Istanbul Regional Hub, the session was a powerful reminder of the delicate balance needed to decarbonize economies while prioritizing inclusive governance and growth. 💡

Panelists acknowledged challenges including the region’s continued reliance on fossil fuels, projected to make up 90% of the energy mix by 2035, and the substantial portion of GDP spent on subsidies. Yet, discussions were focused on identifying promising strategies already in place:

1. The rise of tailored financial instruments to mitigate risks,
2. ⁠digital innovations that identify investment hotspots and optimize resource allocation,
3. ⁠and collaborative policy efforts to unify stakeholders.

A key takeaway was the critical need for a people-centered approach that goes beyond technical measures. The path forward demands adaptive strategies, enhanced regional collaboration, and coordinated efforts to ensure the energy transition leads to an inclusive, long-term systemic transformation. ⚡️
Dr. Pilvi Torsti

caption:
This week, on the sidelines of #COP29, Pradeep Kurukulasuriya  and I had the pleasure of meeting with Gloria Magombo, Permanent Secretary of the Ministry of Energy & Power Development, Zimbabwe, along with other ministry dignitaries. 🫱🏽‍🫲🏼

Our discussions focused on exploring financing mechanisms for scaling off-grid minigrids across 10 identified sites and strategies to accelerate renewable energy deployment in underserved areas. We reviewed the bankability of five sites with completed feasibility studies and outlined next steps for securing funding and implementation.

We emphasized leveraging United Nations Capital Development Fund (UNCDF)  and UNDP  ‘s  expertises, funding, and ongoing support in Zimbabwe’s energy sector, particularly through the Energy Offer project, which focuses on advancing sustainable, off-grid solutions for rural communities. This initiative is designed to accelerate access to sustainable, affordable energy and drive innovative financing for a green economy. 💡


These collaborative efforts are crucial for bridging energy access gaps and aligning with Zimbabwe’s goal of a 33% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030.

caption:
It was an honor to meet with the Iran Renewable Energy Association (IrREA)  during #COP29, building on the UNDP Sustainable Energy Hub  high-level mission to Iran in September.

Our discussions focused on exchanging strategies and leveraging opportunities to accelerate Iran’s energy transition pathway, emphasizing the private sector's key role and innovative financial mechanisms to support Iran’s ambitious target of 30GW renewable energy capacity by 2030. 

We also discussed opportunities to expand international cooperation to scale targeted specialized training programs and regional initiatives to build capacity and equip stakeholders with practical tools for sustainable energy solutions such as energy  efficiency and e-mobility. These efforts aim to help Iran achieve its goal of reducing electrical power consumption by at least 10,000 MW through energy efficiency measures and accelerate a just energy transition. 💡

#SustainableEnergyRevolution #EnergyForDevelopment #Iran #EnergyTransition

Very privileged to have met with H.E. @Fekitamoeloa' Utoikamanu, the Minister of Meteorology, Energy, Information, Disaster Management, Environment, Climate Change, and Communications (MEIDECC) for Tonga, on the sidelines of #COP29 in Azerbaijan last week.

We had a great discussion on implementing UNDP’s SIDS Energy Strategy — aiming for 70% renewable electricity generation by 2030 through energy efficiency measures. This implementation is a key response to the priority of operationalizing the ABAS to advance Tonga’s energy transition.

Achieving Tonga’s targets requires catalytic investments and strategic partnerships to transform the country’s energy infrastructure.

UNDP remains committed to supporting Tonga by strengthening national roadmaps, providing tailored technical expertise and policy guidance, and catalyzing access to private and public sector financing to drive development, energy, and climate breakthroughs.

Excellent meeting with Richard Nelson  Power Africa Coordinator at COP29 Azerbaijan  to discuss actionable pathways for advancing energy solutions in Africa. ⚡️

Key takeaways from our discussion:

1. Identifying new collaboration opportunities to scale clean energy solutions and drive a just energy transition across the continent, ensuring no community is left behind.
2. Partnering to scale up energy financing in Africa by employing innovative mechanisms such as concessional finance, blended finance models, and de-risking strategies to effectively attract and mobilize private sector investments.
3. Leveraging existing initiatives, including UNDP’s Africa Minigrids Program  alongside joint efforts such as Mission 300—a collaboration involving the The World Bank  African Development Bank Group  and other partners—to expand energy access and impact across the continent.

With its integrated approach and strategic partnerships portfolio, UNDP  stands ready to continue supporting Africa’s energy-for-development pathway. 💡

We look forward to working with partners and stakeholders to drive the energy investments the world urgently needs. 🌍

caption:
Desertification affects 52% of agricultural land, costing 10% of global GDP and threatening food and water security for over 2.6 billion people. This demands urgent, transformative investments in integrated solutions across the water-energy-food nexus.

At COP16, I had the privilege of moderating a session co-hosted by UNDP, UNCDF, ICC Saudi Arabia, and Desert Technologies, where leaders from the financial sector, private sector, and public sector explored a key question: How can we catalyze investments in sustainable energy for land and water management to build resilience and unlock development opportunities?

💡 Key Takeaways:

1️⃣ Financial Institutions: Innovative mechanisms such as blended finance, green bonds, and guarantees are essential to de-risk investments, mobilize capital, and scale solutions in high-risk regions.

2️⃣ Private Sector: The private sector plays a pivotal role in developing bankable renewable energy projects, mitigating risks, and fostering sustainable growth.

3️⃣ Media as a Catalyst: By amplifying success stories, media bridges gaps between stakeholders and beneficiaries, driving collective action and highlighting community resilience.

Partnerships among financial institutions, sovereign wealth funds like Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, and international organizations are vital. These multi-sector collaborations are key to combating desertification, restoring ecosystems, and ensuring resilient livelihoods. 🌱

Our conversations at COP16 reaffirmed this: Innovative energy finance is not just an imperative—it’s an opportunity for a resilient future.

#COP16Riyadh #OurLandOurFuture #EnergyTransition #EnergyForDevelopment⚡️

caption:
For the first time in 15 years, we have a new climate finance goal — but is it enough, and more importantly, does it respond to the ambitions of the UAE consensus on clean energy adopted in COP28?  🌎
 
As we close out 2024 and reflect on progress made and the work still ahead, we are sharing this special edition bulletin on financing the sustainable energy revolution 👉  https://lnkd.in/eRFEfQdq
 
The New Collective Quantified Goal adopted at COP29 committed $300 billion per year by 2035, which marks a step forward in mobilizing resources. However, developing nations need annual investment to rise from $770 billion in 2022 to $2.2–2.8 trillion by the early 2030s.
Delivering the COP28 commitments on tripling renewables and doubling energy efficiency depends on bold reforms and collaborative innovation to close the energy finance gap and achieve a just energy transition. 💡
 
Beyond mobilizing private capital and creating a strong enabling environment through policy de-risking to scaling the quantity, focus must shift to the quality and impact of financing. Resources need to be accessible, strategically allocated, and equitably distributed to the regions and populations that need them most. Innovations in digital technologies, data, and AI also play a key role, reducing costs, optimizing resources, and de-risking investments. 📈
 
Happy holidays to our entire sustainable energy family! ⚡️
 
Here’s to continuing our efforts together for a just and impactful energy transition in the year to come. 
 
#EnergyRevolution #EnergyForDevelopment ⚡️#GlobalFinance #EnergyTransition

At the closing high level panel of the IRENA Youth Forum, we saw firsthand how youth are leading innovation and advancing clean energy solutions across the globe. 

To scale this impact, we need more than isolated efforts—we need inclusive, action-driven approaches that prioritize youth-led initiatives. By 2030, investments in the Global South need to triple to meet growing energy demands, and youth must be central to these transformations. 

Initiatives like #Youth4Climate, Green Growth and Jobs Accelerator Programme are designed to provide young people with the tools, training, and networks they need to lead in a just energy transitions. 

Youth is not a phase; they are leading up to the sustainable energy revolution. It’s time to turn pledges into action and ensure youth are at the forefront of this global transformation. Let’s act now for real, lasting change. #IRENA15A #EnergyforDevelopment #SustainableEnergyRevolution

caption:
2024 reminded us of the dual crises shaping our world—a record-breaking year for global temperatures and a pivotal year for renewable energy progress. Clean energy investments surpassed $2 trillion, and renewables outpaced fossil fuels. Yet, these advancements remain unevenly distributed, with low- and middle-income countries capturing only 15% of global clean energy investments (excluding China). 

This stark inequity underscores an urgent opportunity: accelerating the energy transition to drive inclusive growth and decisive climate action. 

I had the privilege of participating in the 15th IRENA Assembly on Innovative Renewables Risk Mitigation Instruments, where key stakeholders convened to explore solutions for scaling investments in underserved markets.  

💡 Key Takeaways from the Assembly: 
 
1️⃣ Lowering Financing Costs: High interest rates disproportionately impact renewable projects. Complementing fiscal strategies with non-fiscal tools—such as guarantees and concessional funding—can attract investment in high-risk markets 
2️⃣ Smarter Risk Mitigation mechanism: Governments in developing countries need support through innovative tools like green bonds, debt-for-clean-energy swaps, and public-private partnerships, which de-risk investments and attract private capital. 
3️⃣ Harnessing Digital Innovations: The integration of geospatial analytics and AI, such as the Clean Energy Equity Index, ensures smarter, data-driven investment decisions that prioritize equity and efficiency. 

As we approach major milestones like COP30 in Brazil and the G20 under South Africa’s leadership, the urgency to mobilize capital, strengthen local systems, and foster strategic partnerships cannot be overstated. 

Together, let us drive a sustainable energy revolution that bridges gaps, unlocks opportunities, and accelerates the transition to clean energy for all. 

#IRENA15A #EnergyforDevelopment

caption:
Antigua and Barbuda is leading the way in advancing a just energy transition. With 23% savings from reduced fossil fuel imports—equivalent to approximately $60 million annually—and an ambitious target of achieving 100% renewable energy by 2030, the country is poised to deliver transformative benefits for its people and the planet.

I had the privilege of meeting H.E. Minister of Energy, Hon. Melford Nicholas, to discuss implementing the ABAS principles. Our discussions focused on key strategies to accelerate this transition while promoting inclusive growth and climate resilience:

1️⃣ Innovative Financial Mechanisms: Exploring options such as guarantee schemes and concessional loans to attract international investment. Collaborations between UNDP and United Nations Capital Development Fund (UNCDF)  aim to maximize these opportunities.

2️⃣ Digitalization for Energy Transition: Utilizing digital technologies to enhance renewable energy integration and enable e-mobility solutions.

3️⃣ Innovative Energy Storage Solutions: Implementing advanced storage systems to manage peak demand and stabilize the grid.

Antigua and Barbuda is a shining example of leadership in sustainable development and climate action. UNDP  is at the forefront to support this journey toward a sustainable energy revolution. 💡✨

To meet SDG7 targets by 2030, we need to provide electricity to 157 million more people and clean cooking solutions to 334 million annually. This requires $3 to $4.5 trillion in annual investments—not just to close gaps but as an opportunity to drive inclusive growth, create jobs, and improve lives. 

At the 15th IRENA Assembly, I had the honor of delivering opening remarks on Sustainable Energy: The Road Ahead. With global energy demand rising as the population grows by 25%, we have a unique opportunity to lift 1.18 billion people out of energy poverty while accelerating a cleaner, more sustainable future. 

Actions for a Sustainable Energy Revolution

1. Scale up financing: Mobilize $3–4.5 trillion annually, shift investments to the Global South, and eliminate market inefficiencies and regulatory barriers. 

2. Innovative finance in the Global South: Support initiatives like Mission 300, Energy for Growth, and the Africa Minigrids Program to expand energy access, accelerate the transition, and create opportunities for inclusive growth. 

3. Leverage digital, data, and AI: Geospatial tools like the UNDP-IBM Clean Energy Equity Index can identify investment opportunities, optimize energy systems, and ensure an equitable energy transition. 

The energy transition is a powerful opportunity to create a brighter, more inclusive future. Together, let’s champion a sustainable energy revolution that benefits everyone, everywhere. 

#IRENA15A #SDG7 #EnergyforDevelopment.

To meet SDG7 targets by 2030, we need to provide electricity to 157 million more people and clean cooking solutions to 334 million annually. This requires $3 to $4.5 trillion in annual investments—not just to close gaps but as an opportunity to drive inclusive growth, create jobs, and improve lives. 

At the 15th IRENA Assembly, I had the honor of delivering opening remarks on Sustainable Energy: The Road Ahead. With global energy demand rising as the population grows by 25%, we have a unique opportunity to lift 1.18 billion people out of energy poverty while accelerating a cleaner, more sustainable future. 

Actions for a Sustainable Energy Revolution

1. Scale up financing: Mobilize $3–4.5 trillion annually, shift investments to the Global South, and eliminate market inefficiencies and regulatory barriers. 

2. Innovative finance in the Global South: Support initiatives like Mission 300, Energy for Growth, and the Africa Minigrids Program to expand energy access, accelerate the transition, and create opportunities for inclusive growth. 

3. Leverage digital, data, and AI: Geospatial tools like the UNDP-IBM Clean Energy Equity Index can identify investment opportunities, optimize energy systems, and ensure an equitable energy transition. 

The energy transition is a powerful opportunity to create a brighter, more inclusive future. Together, let’s champion a sustainable energy revolution that benefits everyone, everywhere. 

#IRENA15A #SDG7 #EnergyforDevelopment.

In 2022, developed countries mobilized $115.9 billion for climate finance, but the efficiency of these investments is declining. Private co-financing per public dollar fell to just 24 cents, down from 51 cents in 2013. 

How can we make every dollar work smarter to catalyze systemic change? 

On the first day of the 15th IRENA Assembly, it was a pleasure to speak at the Ministerial Roundtable on Scaling Up Finance to Support the Energy Transition in Emerging Markets and Developing Economies. 

To address the financing gap, we must act decisively: 

1- Lower the cost of capital for clean energy in EMDEs through de-risking mechanisms, blended finance, and performance-based instruments. 

2- Streamline international support by creating strategic alliances and deepening collaboration for bankable projects, unlocking a $65 billion investment opportunity to connect 265 million people to clean energy. 

3- Leverage tryptic of digital data and AI to optimize investment decisions, accelerating renewable projects and ensuring equitable energy access for local communities. 

Together, through smarter and more impactful investments, we can bridge the financing gap and drive an inclusive, sustainable energy transformation. 

#IRENA15A #EnergyforDevelopment #SustainableEnergyRevolution

caption:
SIDS face a unique energy challenge: 90% fossil fuel reliance, 3x higher electricity costs, and extreme climate vulnerability. But renewable energy offers a pathway to self-reliance, climate resilience, and economic growth. 🌱⚡ 

To unlock this potential, international partners should focus on 3 areas: 

1️⃣ Innovative Financing: #SIDS 🏝️ need $5.9B annually for renewable energy. With debt-for-energy swaps and blended finance, SIDS can save $3.3B annually in reduced fossil fuel imports. 

2️⃣ Capacity Building & SIDS-SIDS Cooperation: Knowledge exchanges and regional partnerships, like floating solar, help integrate renewables at scale. 

3️⃣ Digital Transformation: AI, IoT, and data analytics enable smarter energy systems. Initiatives like CloudSolar in Barbados democratize solar access and empower local investments. 

Guided by the #Antigua and Barbuda Agenda for SIDS, we must drive ‘disruptive innovation’ and take collective action to turn a sustainable, equitable energy future into reality—one that meets today’s needs and enables future generations to build the future they envision. 🌍💡 

#IRENA15A #EnergyforDevelopment #SustainableEnergyRevolution #RisingUpForSIDS

caption:
Today, at the margins of the Fifteenth Session of the International Renewable Energy Agency (IRENA)  Assembly and the World Future Energy Summit, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and United Nations Capital Development Fund (UNCDF)  had hosted a vital side event on a Multi-stakeholder Innovative Energy Finance to Accelerate the Energy Transition in Developing Countries, and I had the privilege of moderating a disruptive and insightful discussion that brought together intergovernmental representatives, development partners, and private sector experts to explore key solutions to unlock the capital needed to accelerate the energy transition in developing countries. 

Here are three critical takeaways from today’s session: 

- Innovative Financing Mechanisms Are Key to Scaling Up: To close the $2.8 trillion investment gap for clean energy in developing countries, we must scale up blended finance, green bonds, and debt-for-energy swaps, complemented by nation-led energy strategies to ensure alignment with local needs and priorities. 

- Strengthening South-South Collaboration: The energy transition requires inclusive, cross-border collaboration, with initiatives like Mission 300, Africa Minigrid Program, and ETAF playing a crucial role in unlocking finance for high-risk markets, particularly in Africa and SIDS, where urgent energy access is needed. 

- Leveraging Digital and Data Technologies to Transform the Energy Landscape: Digital tools like AI and data analytics are transforming energy finance, enabling smarter decision-making, reducing risks, and optimizing energy systems to integrate renewables and improve efficiency while ensuring equity and sustainability. 

This discussion reminded us that closing the financing gap requires collaboration, innovation, and data-driven strategies to ensure an inclusive and equitable sustainable energy revolution. I would like to thank all our distinguished panelists for their continued dedication to ensure just energy transition. 

#EnergyforDevelopment #SustainableEnergyRevolution

caption:
Achieving Africa’s energy and climate goals by 2030 requires over USD 200 billion in annual investments. To achieve this, we must implement clear strategies and secure increased international financial and technical support. 

I had the pleasure of meeting with Power Africa’s Cullen Hughes, Deputy Coordinator, and Carolyn Laurenzano, Development Partnerships Officer, to discuss how we can accelerate a just and equitable energy transition across the continent. Here are the key actions for progress:

1. Developing Pipeline of Bankable Projects: Initiatives like Mission 300, which aims to connect 300 million people in Sub-Saharan Africa to electricity by 2030, and the Africa Minigrids Program, a $65 billion opportunity, are critical for bridging financing gaps. 

2. Integrated Approach to Energy Transition: Unreliable power impacts life-saving services—half of Sub-Saharan Africa’s health facilities lack reliable electricity. Through Power Africa’s the Health Electrification and Telecommunications Alliance (HETA) and UNDP's Solar for Health, we are integrating energy and health to advance universal health coverage. 

3. Innovative Financing for Off-Grid Solutions: Over 60 million people in Africa already access electricity through off-grid solutions. To accelerate energy access, we need innovative financial models and business mechanisms to scale renewable off-grid energy. 

This is a call for urgent, collective action. Together, we can drive unprecedented progress in Africa through sustainable energy transformation. 

#EnergyforDevelopment #SustainableEnergyRevolution

Achieving Africa’s energy and climate goals by 2030 requires over USD 200 billion in annual investments. To achieve this, we must implement clear strategies and secure increased international financial and technical support. 

I had the pleasure of meeting with Power Africa’s Cullen Hughes, Deputy Coordinator, and Carolyn Laurenzano, Development Partnerships Officer, to discuss how we can accelerate a just and equitable energy transition across the continent. Here are the key actions for progress:

1. Developing Pipeline of Bankable Projects: Initiatives like Mission 300, which aims to connect 300 million people in Sub-Saharan Africa to electricity by 2030, and the Africa Minigrids Program, a $65 billion opportunity, are critical for bridging financing gaps. 

2. Integrated Approach to Energy Transition: Unreliable power impacts life-saving services—half of Sub-Saharan Africa’s health facilities lack reliable electricity. Through Power Africa’s the Health Electrification and Telecommunications Alliance (HETA) and UNDP's Solar for Health, we are integrating energy and health to advance universal health coverage. 

3. Innovative Financing for Off-Grid Solutions: Over 60 million people in Africa already access electricity through off-grid solutions. To accelerate energy access, we need innovative financial models and business mechanisms to scale renewable off-grid energy. 

This is a call for urgent, collective action. Together, we can drive unprecedented progress in Africa through sustainable energy transformation. 

#EnergyforDevelopment #SustainableEnergyRevolution

This transition offers a unique opportunity to create green jobs and foster a conducive environment for investment in the renewable energy sector. 

I had the privilege of meeting Iran's deputy Energy Minister, Mohsen Tarztalab to discuss Iran’s energy transition strategy, focusing on key pillars for success: 

1. Develop robust regulatory frameworks, enhance workforce training, and implement support systems to ensure a just and inclusive transition. 

2. Scale sustainable finance through policies that unlock investment in renewables and improve energy efficiency. 

3. Leverage digital innovation and AI to optimize systems and drive data-driven policymaking for broader socio-economic impact. 

This journey will be driven by the convergence of digitalization, market development, policy, and governance. UNDP is proud to be at the forefront, supporting Iran’s sustainable energy transition through collaboration, on-the-ground impact, and tailored solutions. 

#EnergyforDevelopment

Renewables now outpace fossil electricity investment by 10 to 1, with more investment in solar than all other power sources combined.  
 
We are witnessing a sustainable energy revolution. Yet, much remains to be done.  
 
As countries update their NDCs, aligning national strategies with the global goal to triple renewable capacity by 2030 is critical. This requires comprehensive plans addressing all greenhouse gases, a just fossil fuel phase-out, and significant action to unlock $3.8 trillion in annual investment.  
 
Achieving this transition requires global collaboration to direct financial resources toward the areas that need them most—emerging markets and developing economies. 
 
On this International Day of Clean Energy, let's make 2025 the year to ACT: The Future is not only Clean, it must be Just for Everyone.  💡☀️
 
#EnergyForDevelopment⚡️ #EnergyTransition

3️⃣ Mobilizing finance through innovative mechanisms and financial de-risking to close the $3.8 trillion investment gap; and 
4️⃣ Expanding decentralized renewable energy to reverse the recent setbacks in energy access.

caption:
In recent years, digitalization has shifted from being an optional add-on to a cornerstone of the energy sector, driving transformative changes; and 2025 will be no different.

But the rapid digitalization of energy systems also brings complex risks like cybersecurity threats, data bias and ethical concerns that must be proactively managed. The European Union's experience, which saw over 200 cyberattacks on energy infrastructure in 2023 alone, highlights the urgent need for resilient energy systems. 

Protecting critical energy services from these vulnerabilities requires robust governance and security measures. Global collaborative initiatives like the G20's Data20 are steps toward promoting better data governance to support AI-driven innovation and the SDGs.

Moving forward, the challenge will be balancing digital innovation with safeguards to protect infrastructure and ensure equitable access.  

Learn how robust governance can ensure AI and digitalization strengthen—not compromise—the energy transition in 2025, safeguarding infrastructure, data integrity, and equitable access. 👉 bit.ly/seh-bulletin-2025

Achieving SDG 7 in the digital age
 
As we reach the halfway mark towards the 2030 deadline for achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the significance of ‘energy’ as the cornerstone to facing the challenges and opportunities that we face today cannot be overstated. With rising energy demands and environmental concerns, there's an urgent need for cleaner and more inclusive energy solutions. 

Enter digitalization—a transformative force in the energy sector. 

Key insights:
1. Decarbonization Potential: Digital tools can significantly reduce emissions in high-emitting industries, including the energy sector.

2. Enhanced Energy Access: Technologies like geospatial tools and blockchain can optimize energy planning and financing, bringing power to underserved communities.

3. Operational Efficiency: AI and machine learning predict equipment failures, while drones inspect energy assets, ensuring optimal performance.

By integrating digital solutions, we can ensure a cleaner, more sustainable and equitable future for everyone everywhere. 

See here to find out more 👉 https://rb.gy/2h1gnf 

To keep up to date with the latest energy developments, subscribe to the UNDP Sustainable Energy Bulletin here 👉 https://rb.gy/kknhnr

Digital, data, and AI for the future of sustainable energy 🔋🌍 

As we continue to navigate this important decade for sustainable development and climate action, the UAE consensus to triple renewable energy capacity and double energy efficiency improvements by 2030 sets out a clear agenda.  

With global energy demand projected to increase by 18% by 2050, integrating digital technologies (such as AI and data analytics) across the entire energy value chain is crucial. While leading to significant energy efficiency gains and cost savings, digital technological integration could also result in:

➡️ Emission Reduction: If scaled effectively, digital technologies could reduce emissions by up to 20% across the energy, materials, and mobility sectors by 2050 - the three largest contributors to global emissions. 

➡️ Efficiency Boost: Digital tools can identify optimal investment opportunities and guide smart(er) decision-making in renewable energy. 

➡️ Data-Driven Insights: Digital tools can leverage significant amounts of data outputs from the energy transition, which could help address pre-existing social, economic and environmental challenges. 

To find out why digital innovation could be the “low-hanging fruit” to offer a fast and cost-effective solution to accelerate the sustainable energy transition, I invite you to read my @illuminem article available here: 👉 https://rb.gy/mj98ex

caption:
World Energy Day: Ensuring Access to Sustainable Energy for All 🔋💡

With today, as World Energy Day, marked as a time to reflect on “energy efficiency and production alternatives”, it is also important to consider how we, as a global community, recognize the value and importance of sustainable energy.

The COP28 UAE Consensus to Triple Renewable capacity and Double Efficiency by 2030 sets out a clear agenda. Yet at the core of these developments are communities and people — those who still lack their fundamental right to sustainable energy.⚡️

Today, nearly:

➡️ 1.18 billion people live in energy poverty.

➡️ 685 million people live without electricity access.

➡️ 2.1 billion people lacking access to fundamental clean cooking facilities.

➡️ 2 billion people live in conflict-affected areas where energy security is critical.

➡️ Nearly 1 billion people in the Global South lack electricity in healthcare facilities.

As countries update their NDCs for COP30, and the G20 presidency seeks to mobilize finance for a just energy transition, 2025 presents a critical opportunity to move from intent to impactful action.
 
We need to ensure that resources are accessible, strategically allocated, and equitably distributed to those who need them most. Sustainable energy is not only a component of the SDG7 Agenda —“Ensure access to affordable, reliable, sustainable, and modern energy for all” — it is also a key enabler of the entire 2030 Agenda. 🌐

To out why, on this World Energy Day 2025, we must recognize the value and importance of a sustainable energy revolution, I invite you to read this latest edition of the Sustainable Energy Bulletin: 👉 bit.ly/411usOI
 
#EnergyForDevelopment #JustTransition #WorldEnergyDay

caption:
Solid-State Batteries and The Future of Mobility 🔋🚀

As we move towards a more sustainable energy future, Solid-State Batteries (SSBs) are set to transform electric vehicles; renewable energy storage; and public transport. Unlike traditional lithium-ion batteries, SSBs use a solid electrolyte as opposed to a liquid one, offering higher energy density, improved safety, and longer lifecycle.🔋

But why Solid-State Batteries?

➡️ Higher Energy Density: Delivering 5X more energy for the same weight as conventional batteries, making them ideal for industrial applications.

➡️ Faster Charging Times: Fully charged in 10-15 minutes, unlike lithium-ion batteries.

➡️ Safer and More Stable: Addressing fire and safety concerns by using non-flammable solid materials.

➡️ 30-40% Weight Reduction: Improving the overall efficiency of the devices or vehicles they power.

➡️ 10-100 Hours of Energy Storage: Important for improving grid security and building resilient infrastructures for developing countries.

➡️ Lower Carbon Footprint: Using far fewer critical minerals like cobalt & nickel, reducing their overall climate impact by up to 39%.

Find out why, with the right investments and continued innovation, a future powered by clean and renewable energy is within reach in my latest interview with Arval Mobility Observatory: 👉 https://rb.gy/7vrjft 

#EnergyForDevelopment #SolidStateBatteries #FutureOfMobility #EnergyStorage
Woochong Um Marcos Neto Damilola Ogunbiyi
